summary: Verification result for 2026-10-26: no next-gen drug has a trial result or regulatory step that first became public in the last 48 hours, so there is no Lane C news today. What I checked: retatrutide's latest regulatory step is the FDA's Oct 2 remand decision (Seventh Circuit appeal argued Sept 24, still pending; Lilly's filing planned Q1 2027). Survodutide SYNCHRONIZE-2 was in NEJM on Oct 1. CagriSema's women post hoc came out Oct 20. Pfizer's monthly PF-08653944 data date from Feb/June. Corxel's Oct 26 news about CX11 is a stock-market merger deal; the CX11 Phase 2 data were first reported June 23, so it doesn't qualify. The one big catalyst in sight is the CagriSema FDA decision, expected in Q4 2026 (window opened Oct 1, US launch planned early 2027). Pre-build a Lane P 'What Is CagriSema?' decoder now and turn it into a same-day Lane C video when the decision lands. On no-news days, follow the playbook's Lane A: (1) tirzepatide and hair loss, which has strong search demand and an evidence base (BMJ Penn cohort, Jul 2026: 6.91 vs 5.04 per 1,000 person-years against SGLT-2, non-scarring; FAERS signals for tirzepatide and semaglutide; about 400 MHRA tirzepatide reports in 2026); (2) the body-worry test long-form on bones, muscle and hair (Arch Osteoporos Oct 23 review plus the Oct 19 handgrip meta-analysis); (3) stopping tirzepatide (SURMOUNT-4); (4) protein on tirzepatide; (5) Thanksgiving on tirzepatide, best published around Nov 10–20. For Shorts: a nausea-measurement body-worry Short (DOM Oct 22), and a retatrutide 'what's confirmed?' Short on the drug-vs-biologic dispute. Reject anything on microdosing, research-grade retatrutide sourcing or switching from compounded products. Cost/Medicare, indirect-comparison 'beats' framing and observational surgery angles are left out under the playbook bans.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and hair loss: how common, and what helps? BMJ Penn cohort (Jul 2026: GLP-1 users had 37% higher adjusted risk of alopecia than SGLT-2 users, 6.91 vs 5.04 per 1,000 person-years, mostly non-scarring), FAERS alopecia signals for tirzepatide and semaglutide, about 400 MHRA tirzepatide hair-loss reports in 2026
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, honest uncertainty: 'Tirzepatide and Hair Loss: How Common and What Helps'. Absolute numbers first (about 7 vs 5 per 1,000 people a year). Observational = 'linked to'. Non-scarring means follicles stay intact and regrowth is possible. Explain the likely link to rapid weight loss and low intake (telogen effluvium), then what helps: protein, overall nutrition, and checking iron or other levels with a clinician. Note that the BMJ cohort was adults with type 2 diabetes on the GLP-1 class, while FAERS is a reporting-signal database. No supplement promises.

candidates.why_now: The playbook names it as a Lane A example. Body-worry topics are our best cross-platform format (bones Short 228, Instagram body-worry median reach 112). UK MHRA report counts keep the topic in UK news. High-CPM search phrase with long tail.
